needs: A metaphor: a coat check with numbered hooks stands in for a hash table, then is relabelled.

brief.title: A hash table is a coat check
brief.idea: A hash table works like a coat check: a rule turns each key into a hook number, so finding a value means going straight to one hook instead of searching every coat.

beats.say: A coat check has ten numbered hooks. Hand over a coat with your name, and the attendant hangs it on one.
beats.show: A row of ten hooks numbered 0 to 9 appears behind a counter.

beats.say: The trick is the rule for choosing a hook: add up the places of the letters in the alphabet, and keep the last digit.
beats.show: A card shows the rule: letter positions are added, and the last digit is kept.

beats.say: Leo is twelve, five and fifteen, which adds to thirty two, so his coat goes on hook two.
beats.show: The name Leo splits into 12, 5 and 15, the sum 32 appears, and a coat moves onto hook 2.

beats.say: Ana is one, fourteen and one, which adds to sixteen, so her coat goes on hook six.
beats.show: The name Ana becomes 16, and a coat moves onto hook 6.

beats.say: When Leo comes back, the attendant runs the same rule, gets two, and walks straight to that hook.
beats.show: The name Leo turns into 2 again and the attendant goes directly to hook 2, passing the others.

beats.say: Zoe adds to forty six, which also ends in six. Two names, one hook: that is a collision.
beats.show: The name Zoe becomes 46, and her coat heads for hook 6, where the coat of Ana already hangs.

beats.say: The attendant hangs both coats on hook six and reads the tags there, still only two to check.
beats.show: Both coats hang together on hook 6, each with its name tag showing.

beats.say: In a program the names are keys, the hooks are slots in an array, and the rule is the hash function.
beats.show: The labels change: names become keys, hooks become array slots 0 to 9, and the rule card becomes hash().

beats.say: So finding a value takes one quick calculation and one slot, not a search through every coat.
beats.show: One key is hashed and a single slot lights up, while the other slots stay dark.

beats.say: That is why finding one name among a million keys takes about as long as finding it among ten.
beats.show: The row of slots stretches to a million, and still a single slot lights up.
